_meta.name: thursday-ai-tool-surface
_meta.description: Thursday AI's platform-agnostic action vocabulary. 26 tools. Each is dispatched by the runtime to OS-specific primitives (pyautogui, xdotool, AppleScript, Win UI Automation). One tool call per assistant turn.

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Launch a desktop application by friendly name. The runtime resolves the name to the OS-appropriate launcher (e.g. 'firefox' -> firefox.exe / firefox / open -a Firefox). Use this when the user wants to start an app.

args.description: Optional command-line arguments to pass to the app.

tools.name: close_window
tools.description: Close the currently focused window. Equivalent to Alt+F4 (Win/Linux) or Cmd+W (macOS). Destructive: if the window has unsaved work, the runtime asks the user to confirm.

force.description: If true, skip user confirmation. Reserved for cases where the model has just verified the window is safe to close.

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Bring an application to the foreground by name. Use this instead of multiple Alt+Tab calls.

app_name.description: Friendly name of the application to bring to the foreground.

tools.name: minimize_window
tools.description: Minimize the active window to the taskbar / dock.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click at screen coordinates (x, y) measured in pixels from the top-left of the primary display. Always call screenshot() first to identify the target coordinates. The runtime will use pyautogui on all OSes; on Linux it can fall back to xdotool.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Drag the mouse from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2). Useful for sliders, drag-and-drop, and resizing windows.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type a string into the currently focused input field. The text is sent as a sequence of keypresses, so existing content is appended unless the user has selected-all first. For replacing content, call key_press(keys='ctrl+a') first.

tools.name: key_press
tools.description: Press a single key or a hotkey combination. Use pyautogui-style names: 'enter', 'esc', 'tab', 'space', 'backspace', 'ctrl+c', 'ctrl+v', 'cmd+shift+4', 'alt+f4', 'win+d', etc. On macOS, 'cmd' is the meta key.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the focused window by N wheel-notches. Positive scrolls down, negative scrolls up. Use this to navigate long pages.

amount.description: Number of wheel-notches to scroll. Negative scrolls up.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current screen. Returns the path to the saved PNG plus OCR'd text and the title of the focused window. ALWAYS call this before clicking or typing into a UI you cannot see, so you have current coordinates.

region.description: Optional sub-region of the screen to capture instead of the full screen.

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List files and subdirectories in a directory. Returns a JSON array of {name, type:'file'|'dir', size_bytes}. Use this to explore the filesystem before read_file or write_file.

path.description: Absolute path to a directory. Use '~' for the user home dir (the runtime expands it).

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read up to 64 KB of a text file. Returns the content as a string. For binary files, use run_shell with a tool like 'file' or 'xxd'.

offset.description: Byte offset to start reading from.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write text to a file. Overwrites if the file exists. DESTRUCTIVE: the runtime will ask the user to confirm via voice before executing, unless the user has pre-approved the path in their config.

tools.name: run_shell
tools.description: Run a shell command and return the exit code plus combined stdout/stderr (truncated to 8 KB). DESTRUCTIVE if the command mutates state (rm, mv, sudo, etc.). The runtime confirms with the user unless the command matches a per-session allowlist (ls, cat, pwd, git status, etc.).

cmd.description: Shell command. Use the OS-appropriate shell (bash on Linux/macOS, cmd or powershell on Windows).

cwd.description: Working directory. Defaults to the user's home.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open the user's default web browser. If a URL is given, navigate to it; otherwise open the homepage / new-tab page. Returns the resulting page title and URL.

url.description: Optional URL to navigate to. Must be a fully-qualified URL with scheme.

tools.name: browser_search
tools.description: Run a search query in the browser's default search engine and return the resulting page URL plus the top 5 result titles and URLs. Faster than driving the search bar by hand.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the active browser tab to a URL. Use this after browser_open to move to a specific page.

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description: Close the active browser tab.

tools.name: paste_to_webai
tools.description: Submit a query to Thursday AI's local web-search subsystem (uses the z-ai-web-dev-sdk web_search under the hood). Returns structured search results without opening a browser. Use this when the user just wants information quickly.

tools.name: read_webai_response
tools.description: Fetch the textual content of a URL via Thursday AI's web_reader subsystem. Returns the cleaned article / page text. Faster and cheaper than driving a browser. Use this after browser_search or paste_to_webai to extract page content.

tools.name: set_alarm
tools.description: Create an alarm clock entry at the specified time. Wraps gnome-clocks on Linux, Clock.app on macOS, and Windows Alarms on Windows. Time is local to the system timezone.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for the alarm.

tools.name: set_volume
tools.description: Set the system master volume. Wraps amixer/pactl on Linux, osascript on macOS, CoreAudio on Windows.

tools.name: toggle_mute
tools.description: Toggle mute on the system audio output.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open a URL in the user's default handler. For http(s) URLs this is the browser; for mailto: it is the mail client; for file:// it is the file manager. Use browser_open + browser_navigate if you need to control the browser specifically.

tools.name: notify_user
tools.description: Send a desktop notification (libnotify on Linux, NSUserNotification on macOS, Windows toast). Use this to confirm a background task finished, or to remind the user without speaking aloud.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a clarifying question via voice. Blocks until the user responds. Use this when the goal is ambiguous, when a destructive action needs confirmation, or when the model genuinely does not know how to proceed.

tools.name: finish
tools.description: Signal that the goal is complete. Includes a final summary for the user (kept to ≤ 2 lines unless the user explicitly asked for a long summary). The orchestrator speaks the summary via TTS and clears the working history.

summary.description: Final summary to speak to the user. Keep ≤ 2 lines.
